scope: State-driven optional Compose request list/detail and bounded source/status/query filtering. No transport or app integration.

lock-1.interpretation: Intentional npm lock update, not a source-frozen test acceptance.

strict-10.interpretation: All eight JVM cases passed; missing Android artifact checksums. Screenshot review then found oversized search label and cramped status column with font scale2.

strict-11.interpretation: Reflowed rows and bounded search label passed all eight JVM cases; missing Android host runtime checksums.

strict-12.interpretation: Android host and actual Wasm filter cases passed; missing common metadata artifacts.

strict-17.interpretation: Strict assembly succeeded; reused verified same-source tests, no fresh tests claimed.

strict-2.interpretation: Same missing marker; an earlier failed checksum download did not stop the shell from launching this unnecessary repeat. Preserved as failed, not accepted.

strict-5.interpretation: New Compose module changed npm workspace lock; core JVM/host cases passed before failure.

strict-7.interpretation: Missing JVM UI test runtime checksums.

strict-8.interpretation: Four UI cases failed because this Linux host lacked the generic fonts used by Compose.

strict-9.interpretation: Fonts installed; two UI cases failed because the filter button was 40dp rather than the required 48dp.

testReuse: Final strict17 assembly reused current-source reports; actual fresh Compose runs were strict11 JVM8 and strict12 Android host4/Wasm browser4. No unchanged test rerun solely to manufacture fresh evidence.

environment.linuxFonts: ttf-dejavu 2.37+18+g9b5d1b2f-8 installed from Arch signed package; CI declares fonts-dejavu-core
environment.fontFailure: Compose generic Linux font aliases did not include the only preinstalled Liberation/Adwaita fonts.

initialFetchFailures: Maven plugin marker .sha256 URLs returned404; artifact was verified against published SHA-1 then SHA-256 pinned.

Apple klib Gradle display names differed from published artifact filenames; resolver used the already checksum-verified module metadata to resolve exact names before checking published SHA-1 and pinning SHA-256.
